transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Avery Collins (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Dr. Maya Hernandez, Liam O'Connor, Priya Singh, Noah Kim

Auto-summary (auto-generated): Discussed POC quality evaluation plan; agreed on dataset size, golden prompts, regression tests, hallucination thresholds and 4-week timeline. Action items assigned.

Transcript:
[00:00] Avery: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, really appreciate you making the time. I'm Avery, account lead at Redwood. With me is Samir, our solutions engineer.
[00:08] Samir: Hi all. I'll mostly cover the benchmark details and the eval plan.
[00:12] Dr. Maya: Thanks, Avery. Quick context - we want to pilot LLM-based clinical note summarization and prior-authorization form helpers, PHI will be in scope so security is a big deal. We're exploring hosted first but may require a private deployment.
[00:28] Liam: Also want concrete numbers for latency and hallucination - our clinicians won't accept hallucinations beyond a very low threshold.
[00:35] Avery: Totally understood. Today we want to align on success criteria, workload sizing for the POC, the actual benchmark runs and timelines. We'll propose a quality evaluation plan - golden prompts, regression tests, hallucination/format checks and scoring.
[00:49] Priya: For us, SOC 2 is table stakes. We'll need audit logs, KMS integration, and canton we'll probably need a VPC/private deployment if PHI is involved.
[00:59] Samir: Noted. We'll include both a hosted baseline and a dedicated/private plan in the runbook. For the eval plan itself - thinking of three pillars: accuracy/label-match (entity extraction / summarization overlap), hallucination rate, and format/structure validity (JSON schema / CCD for outputs).
[01:18] Noah: On dataset size - we can provide about 5,000 redacted examples across the two use-cases. Average request size ~120-180 tokens, typical expected response 150-400 tokens but we'll trim for the eval.
[01:31] Samir: Ok that maps well. For throughput sizing - what's realistic for your pilot? QPS? burst patterns?
[01:37] Liam: Initial pilot is low concurrency, maybe 10-20 concurrent clinicians, peak 50 qps for the demo environment. Sustained expected 10 qps.
[01:46] Samir: Great, so we'll design the benchmark to hit peak 50 qps and steady 10 qps. We'll capture p50/p90/p99 latency and per-token cost.
[01:55] Avery: Success criteria - can you confirm the hard gates? e.g. latency under 300ms for p50, under 800ms for p99? and hallucination rate below 2%?
[02:05] Liam: We'd like tighter p50 <200ms ideally, p99 under 600ms. Hallucination target <1-2% for factual fields, higher tolerance for free-text summaries but must be flagged.
[02:17] Dr. Maya: For clinical accuracy, F1 > 0.9 on named-entity extraction (medications, dosages), ROUGE for summaries above 0.65 as a rough number. Also must pass format checks for downstream ingestion - JSON must validate against our schema 100% of the time or errors flagged.
[02:34] Samir: We'll include those as scoring criteria. Our proposal: composite score made of weighted metrics: 40% accuracy (F1/ROUGE), 30% hallucination penalty (lower is better), 20% format/validation pass-rate, 10% latency cost normalized. We can tune weights with you.
[02:53] Priya: How do you detect hallucinations automatically? That's important - clinicians need evidence.
[02:59] Samir: Good question. We'll use a combination: n-gram overlap / entailment checks vs ground truth where available; for factual fields we'll run strict matching against expected values; plus a small manual review sample to estimate false positives/negatives. We'll also add a hallucination classifier threshold and flag outputs that trip it. It's not perfect but it gives a measured rate.
[03:20] Noah: For regression tests, we want to include golden prompts - canonical prompts that should not regress across model upgrades, and a suite of randomized edge cases. Also include negative tests for hallucination-prone cases.
[03:33] Samir: Exactly. We'll define three sets: golden (500 examples), regression (2k examples), and stress/randomized (2.5k examples) totalling 5k. Golden prompts will have strict pass/fail checks. Regression tests will be scored.
[03:46] Avery: On model selection, do you want us to run the POC against our verified open models and a Redwood-optimized private quantized variant? We can also show dedicated-reserved GPU runs for latency comparisons.
[03:58] Liam: Yes - please include a small-hosted baseline (standard open model), a Redwood-optimized variant, and a dedicated GPU run. Need cost and latency tradeoffs.
[04:07] Priya: For security: will the hosted option allow PHI? We can't send raw PHI outside our VPC.
[04:14] Avery: We recommend dedicated/private for PHI. For hosted we can do a redaction layer or encrypted in-transit but typically customers require VPC/private for PHI. We'll include that in the recommendation. We'll also share our SOC 2 docs, KMS integration notes and audit log examples - link in follow-up.
[04:30] Dr. Maya: Timeline-wise what's realistic? We're aiming to kick off next week if possible.
[04:35] Samir: Proposed 4-week POC: Week 0 (onboarding & infra): give us sample data and access (1 week); Week 1 (baseline runs): hosted & open-model baselines; Week 2 (quality evaluations): run golden/regression suites, hallucination checks; Week 3 (optimize & iterate): apply quantization/latency tuning and compile final report and recommendations.
[04:53] Avery: So essentially 4 calendar weeks. We'll commit to a deliverable at the end: final scorecard, cost/latency tradeoff table, and suggested production plan.
[05:02] Liam: What about acceptance? Who signs off?
[05:05] Dr. Maya: I'll be the technical owner for accuracy gating, Priya will sign off on security artifacts, and Liam will make the go/no-go decision.
[05:12] Samir: Great, on the scoring approach - we mentioned a composite score. We'll provide the evaluation spreadsheet showing per-test scoring, weights, and a pass/fail threshold for the POC (e.g., composite >0.75). We can also include model-level fallback rules (if accuracy below X but latency good then fallback to variant).
[05:30] Noah: About format checks - our integration requires a strict CCD/JSON snippet for EHR ingestion. We need 100% syntactic validity; for semantic checks we'll allow warnings but not break the pipeline.
[05:42] Samir: We'll implement two-stage checks: (1) syntactic validation (JSON schema) as gate; (2) semantic confidence score for fields - low confidence flagged for manual triage.
[05:52] Priya: Data residency - we may need EU-only region for certain patients; can Redwood pin region for dedicated pools?
[05:59] Avery: Yes, dedicated & private supports region pinning. We'll note regional latency impact in the runbook.
[06:07] Liam: Cost estimate - can you provide an initial order-of-magnitude for the 4-week POC including dedicated vs hosted?
[06:13] Samir: We'll include a rough cost comparison in the runbook: hosted baseline (pay-as-you-go) vs dedicated reserved short-term pool. I'll include cost per 1k tokens and an estimate for the 5k-run across different configs.
[06:25] Dr. Maya: For golden prompts, we'll need to sign off on them before they become the canonical set. How do you handle updates?
[06:31] Avery: Golden prompts are versioned - we'll freeze a v1 before the evaluation. If you want to add new cases we can append but they won't count against the POC unless we re-run. We'll keep a changelog.
[06:42] Noah: Any gotchas about the transcriptions? my example payloads sometimes include OCR noise, abbreviations - we should include those in stress tests.
[06:49] Samir: Good call - we'll add an OCR-noise subset to the stress tests.
[06:54] Priya: Please include required artifacts list in the follow-up: SOC2 report, network diagram template, encryption-in-transit docs, and our security questionnaire answers.
[07:04] Avery: We'll bundle the Redwood security pack and a redacted runbook link.
[07:08] Dr. Maya: OK great. Let's recap next steps.
[07:12] Avery: Recap: Redwood will send the quality-eval spreadsheet and golden prompt list by Friday 3/6; Samir will send the benchmark runbook and cost estimates by 3/8; Cardinal will provide 5k redacted examples by 3/9; Priya will review security docs by 3/10. We'll schedule the baseline runs for week of 3/9.
[07:30] Liam: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[07:33] Avery: Thanks all, we'll follow up with calendar invites and the doc links.
